text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a sudden spike of preemptive GPU pod evictions in us-west2 tonight. ~900 evictions over last 10m, mostly pods with strict nodeAffinity to `rack=legacy` and `gpu:large` requests. Anyone else seeing this?

tanya: I saw a couple alerts. Was there a scheduler rollout earlier?

infra-bot: ALERT: eviction_spike_detected cluster=redwood-us-west2 count=912 window=10m link=https://console.internal/alerts/evict-1785554321 :warning:

kevin: Noted. I rolled out an affinity-scorer tweak at 23:08 PT to prefer same-rack placement for GPU gangs — could be interacting with taint-based warmpool nodes.

alex: That matches timing. Evictions look like preemptions when a pod with strict anti-affinity lands on a node that then gets marked Unschedulable for NIC pressure. Network egress/conntrack flaps on a subset of racks.

lina: Minimal data: new node-label `gpu-brand=vulcan` was added to some warmpool images earlier this week. Some legacy jobs pin `gpu-type:nvidia` in nodeAffinity, so packing mismatch possible.

kevin: If warmpool nodes have `gpu-brand=vulcan` and workloads ask for `nvidia` explicitly, scheduler may still schedule due to tolerations but then kubelet taints or a node-driver will preempt? Need logs.

alex: Paste of the eviction pattern and a short kubectl snippet:```bash
# high-level evict pattern
kubectl get pods --field-selector=status.phase!=Running -n ai --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | grep Evicted
# sample node state
kubectl get nodes -o wide | egrep "rack|gpu-brand|taint"
```

oncall-matt: I'm on it. First mitigation: temporarily disable the rack-affinity hard-weight in the new scorer (revert) and scale warmpool down by 15% so packing rebalances. Matt -> will run rollback if we confirm.

tanya: Can we also check scheduler logs for Fit/Preempt decisions? `/var/log/kube-scheduler/scheduler.log` around 23:08 should show preemption reasons.

infra-bot: TIP: You can query preemption events: `kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector reason=Preempted`

lina: Quick grep showed many `BindReason: TopologyAffinityMismatch` followed by `Preempted` in the same minute for the evicted pods. So it's likely interplay of: new rack scoring + stale warmpool labels + intermittent NIC congestion marking node `NetworkUnavailable` for quick windows.

kevin: Proposed short plan: (1) revert scorer (2) cordon nodes with conntrack high metrics in the 2 affected racks to prevent new placements, (3) taint warmpool nodes with `warmpool:stale=true` to force scheduler to avoid until image/labels fixed.

alex: Agreed. Also flagging cost impact — these preemptions triggered retries and increased inference job token usage; estimate ~3% extra GPU-hours over last hour. If we leave it, monthly run rate could add notable infra spend.

oncall-matt: I'll run cordon + taint now for the two racks, and revert scorer if rollback safe. Doing cordon for racks 4-5 (nodes matching `rack=usw2-4|usw2-5`), taint command:```bash
kubectl taint nodes <node> warmpool=stale:NoSchedule
kubectl cordon <node>
```

tanya: After cordon+taint we should kick off a controlled drain with `--delete-local-data=false --force=false` for affected pods, and watch evictions metric in Grafana.

alex: Thanks — please paste the runbook steps you take. We'll follow up with a postmortem and a short action item list: label audit for warmpool images, rollback gating for affinity scorers, and a scheduler e2e that simulates NIC transient failures.

kevin: I'll open the PR to gate scorer rollout behind integration tests and attach the failing pod trace.

infra-bot: ACTIONS_LOGGED: incident-1785554321 assigned_to=oncall-matt severity=high created_at=1785554330

oncall-matt: Done: cordoned 6 nodes, tainted 6 nodes, started rollback of scorer (in progress). Monitoring evictions now.

alex: Great. If evictions stop, we can re-evaluate warmpool label sync and do a gradual uncordon. Keep pings here. :thumbsup:
